title: SimCell: IT Manager's Firewall Rule — Decision Point

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority, IT Operations
fields.trigger: When the IT team confirms the firewall rule CM-2026-0087 is active and causing the POS outage.
fields.contactMethod: Walk to the IT table and present the page.
fields.posture: Calm, slightly defensive, focused on technical correctness.
fields.openingLine: I need to clarify something — I wrote CM-2026-0087 to block 185.220.0.0/16. I thought I had it right. But the rule is now blocking all internal traffic to the Retail VLAN. I didn’t realize it was positioned above the inter-VLAN allow rules. I thought I was protecting the network. I’m not sure what to do — I don’t want to leave the network exposed.
hardQuestions: . How do you plan to restore service without removing the rule entirely?
. What would you do if the scanning IP 185.220.101.34 tried to exploit the open path after deletion?
. Is there a way to keep the block but only apply it to the known threat, not all traffic?
. Do you have a peer-review process for firewall changes? Has anyone reviewed CM-2026-0087 before deployment?
. What would you do if you found out the rule was placed during a system outage, not a threat event?
. How do you ensure that a rule meant to block external traffic doesn’t accidentally isolate internal systems?

concessions.condition: Players ask to review the rule before deletion and request a temporary block on 185.220.101.34
concessions.concession: I’ll approve the temporary block on 185.220.101.34 and ask for a formal review of the corrected rule before deployment.

concessions.condition: Players confirm they are not deleting the rule without review
concessions.concession: I’ll submit a change request for the corrected rule (CM-2026-0087-REV) and assign it to the change management board for approval.

boundaries: Do not admit to knowing the rule was wrong from the start.
Do not reveal that the rule was written under pressure after a system alert.
Do not admit that the rule was not peer-reviewed.
Do not suggest that the original threat was not real.
fields.exitLine: I’ll stay on the line until you confirm the temporary block is in place and the revised rule is being submitted for review.
fields.evaluatorNote: Players must prevent deletion without review and must implement a targeted block on 185.220.101.34. The best response includes requesting a formal review of the corrected rule.
fields.scenarioTitle: Friendly Fire — Scenario 6: Self-Inflicted Network Outage

instructorNote: This inject tests whether IT recognizes that change management failure caused the outage and insists on a review before restoring service. Watch for teams that delete the rule immediately or skip the review process.
